analysis.session_summary: The window was dominated by a broad USD bid and a Brent spike on Hormuz/Iran supply headlines, with DXY up 0.289% and Brent up 3.83%. The US data pulse was soft—ISM printed 54.6 vs 55.2—but the USD reaction was muted (-0.031% basket), leaving geopolitics as the main driver. CHF and NZD were the weakest majors, while JPY was near flat despite risk-off, and EUR/GBP was effectively unchanged. Most major legs lacked a single clear catalyst; only the late 'Multiple explosions reported across southern Iran' headline accounted for measurable portions of several late USD and oil moves.

themes.theme: Geopolitical supply shock drives oil and USD
themes.evidence: Brent/USD +3.83%, VIX/USD +1.768%, SPX/USD -0.477%; 'Two Oil Supertankers Hit By Projectiles In Hormuz' and 'Multiple explosions reported across southern Iran' were top headlines.

themes.theme: Hawkish ECB/BoE chatter versus soft inflation data
themes.evidence: ECB's Simkus said 'It is clear that we should hike rates in September'; ECB's Nagel welcomed coordination on yen intervention; BoE's Mann said rates may need to be 'a little bit too high'. Core CPI Flash Estimate y/y printed 2.4% vs 2.5% forecast and was muted.
USD mean vs majors +0.337%; USD/CHF +0.517%, USD/CAD +0.324%, NZD/USD -0.451%, CHF/JPY -0.214%.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD chopped in a 39.3-pip daily range, closing near the low after a late down leg of -21.6 pips, with only the Ueda-Bessent headline adding a measurable 3.4-pip lift in the 10:00-16:00 up leg.
leg_notes.GBP/USD: GBP/USD also ended near its lows (-34.1 pips on the day) after six legs, with a 22.2-pip up move around 15:00 unwound by a -36.1-pip drop into the close.
leg_notes.USD/JPY: USD/JPY pushed to 160.164 (+48.4 pips) in a choppy five-leg tape, with the 02:15-14:30 up leg of 51.1 pips doing most of the work and an ISM-linked -22.4-pip dip only briefly interrupting.
leg_notes.USD/CHF: USD/CHF rose 41.8 pips to 0.81233 in a persistent 46.1-pip up leg from 23:00, closing near the top of a 47.4-pip range.
leg_notes.USD/CAD: USD/CAD rallied 44.9 pips to 1.39048, driven by a 58.9-pip up leg from 02:15, closing at the top of a 61.2-pip range.
leg_notes.AUD/USD: AUD/USD ended down 17.5 pips at 0.7150 after a 39.0-pip down leg from 02:15 was only partly retraced by a 9.5-pip late bounce.
leg_notes.NZD/USD: NZD/USD was the weakest major, down 26.7 pips to 0.58919, with a 35.6-pip down leg from 02:15 and a late 17.8-pip drop after the Iran explosion headlines.
leg_notes.EUR/CHF: EUR/CHF gained 23.3 pips to 0.94111, with the 13:15-16:45 up leg of 30.5 pips only partially pared by a -5.8-pip late slip.
leg_notes.CHF/JPY: CHF/JPY fell 42.2 pips to 197.156 as a -55.8-pip down leg from 13:15 overwhelmed earlier up legs.
leg_notes.AUD/NZD: AUD/NZD rose 25.1 pips to 1.21344, with a 34.5-pip up leg in Asia followed by two-way chop and a final 24.4-pip up leg.

polarity_reads.read: The miss (54.6 vs 55.2) produced only a -0.031% USD basket impulse, inside the noise floor; this says the market was not positioned for a hawkish USD surprise from data and the reaction was dominated by other drivers.

polarity_reads.event: Core CPI Flash Estimate y/y +1 more
polarity_reads.read: The 2.4% vs 2.5% print generated a +0.017% EUR basket impulse—also inside the noise floor—so the data did not validate ECB hawkish chatter, leaving EUR without a fresh catalyst.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical premium extension / USD bid
scenarios.thesis: Hormuz/Iran headlines keep Brent elevated and risk-off supports the USD; no new info forces a reversal, so current strength and weak CHF/NZD persist.
triggers: Additional tanker or southern Iran escalation headlines
scenarios.invalidation: A clear de-escalation or risk-on recovery in SPX/VIX unwinds the USD bid.

pair_paths.rationale: USD bid and close near bottom of daily range.
Risk-off and oil spike keep USD/JPY near high; ISM did not derail.
CHF is weakest major and USD/CHF closed near top of range.
CAD has not benefited from oil; USD/CAD remains bid near 1.39048.

scenarios.name: De-escalation and hawkish ECB/BoE retracement
scenarios.thesis: If Iran headlines fade and risk stabilizes, the USD bid reverses while ECB/BoE hawkish remarks get more weight, lifting European currencies and pressuring USD/JPY.
scenarios.invalidation: New supply disruption or strong US ADP re-asserts the USD.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR close near low and daily range 39.3 leaves room for a bounce to top of range.
GBP closed near low; a bullish catalyst could retrace the day's range.
Ueda/Bessent intervention chatter and safe-haven unwind would drag USD/JPY off highs.
CHF recovers if safe-haven bid rotates out of USD.

scenarios.name: Commodity-bloc / RBNZ-BOC repricing
scenarios.thesis: RBNZ delivers a hawkish 25bp and BOC signals concerns over oil-driven inflation, supporting NZD and CAD against a steadier USD.
triggers: RBNZ OCR hits 2.75% with hawkish statement
scenarios.invalidation: RBNZ surprises dovish or BOC dismisses oil spike; fresh Iran escalation dominates.

pair_paths.rationale: NZD is weakest major (-0.179%) and a hawkish RBNZ could squeeze shorts across its daily range.
CAD has been weak despite Brent +3.83%; BOC hawkish hold could push USD/CAD back down its range.
NZD outperformance vs AUD would reverse the day's 25.1-pip gain and test the daily range.

risks.why_it_matters: Brent already +3.83% and VIX +1.768%; more supply hits can extend USD and oil-risk premium, worsening CHF/NZD underperformance.
risks.watch: Headlines on tanker projectiles and southern Iran explosions; DXY and Brent closes.

risks.why_it_matters: NZD is the weakest major (-0.179%) and the market is likely short; a hawkish or dovish surprise can create outsized moves in NZD/USD and AUD/NZD.
USD/CAD closed near 1.39048 after +44.9 pips despite oil gains; if BOC validates CAD strength, the move could reverse.
risks.watch: BOC rate statement and press conference; Overnight Rate at 15:45.

risks.why_it_matters: After muted ISM (54.6 vs 55.2), a strong ADP could finally move USD and unwind EUR/GBP supportive flows.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: The coming window is shaped by the RBNZ decision (OCR forecast 2.75% vs 2.50%) and BOC hold decision (2.25% expected), both of which can reprice NZD and CAD; AU GDP q/q at 03:30 and US ADP at 14:15 add macro catalysts. Geopolitical headlines from the Hormuz/Iran situation remain the main unknown after Brent and VIX moves.
